chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked him about what is killed by the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? He said: No.

key_terms.الْبُنْدُق: Pellet/bundq — a small clay or stone ball used with a sling or pellet bow; not a sharpened projectile
key_terms.الْحَجَر: Stone — a blunt, non-cutting projectile used to strike game
key_terms.قَتَلَ: Kills — to strike down without the conditions of proper Islamic slaughter

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to eat an animal killed by a stone or pellet?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Muslim asked one of the two Imams (al-Baqir or al-Sadiq, peace be upon them) whether the meat of an animal killed by a thrown stone or pellet (bundq) is permissible to eat. The Imam's answer was a clear and emphatic 'No.' In Islamic jurisprudence, the lawful slaughter (dhabh) of game requires either a sharp cutting instrument or a trained hunting animal; striking game with a blunt projectile or stone does not constitute proper slaughter, making the resulting carcass unlawful (haram) to consume.
word_analysis: can it be eaten/is it permissible to eat

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about what is killed by the stone and the pellet, can one eat from it?’
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam,
about a prey killed with a stone or clay-ball; if it can be used for food. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not edible.’”
